The Strix's card draw is nice but Propaganda's persistent protection is more impactful at this stage. That said, Baleful Strix does draw a card and provide a deathtouch blocker, so this is debatable.

They have Baleful Strix (UB, 2 mana) and Dungeon Map (3 mana) in hand that could have been deployed alongside an evoked Mulldrifter. Additionally, the player has Phantom Steed in hand which could later blink creatures for value, but they also have Sefris as their commander who triggers on creatures going to the graveyard - evoking Mulldrifter would trigger Sefris's dungeon venture ability when it dies. However, since Sefris isn't on the battlefield yet, the graveyard synergy argument doesn't apply right now. The main consideration is tempo: paying full cost leaves no mana for other plays this turn, while evoking would allow deploying another card. With Phantom Steed in hand (which could copy the Mulldrifter if it stayed), keeping the body has some future value. This is debatable but spending all mana on a 2/2 flyer when you could have developed more board presence is slightly questionable.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mulldrifter for full cost {4}{U}, using all available mana
annotations.betterLine: Evoke Mulldrifter for {2}{U} to draw two cards, then use remaining mana to cast Baleful Strix (draw another card and get a 1/1 flying deathtouch blocker) for stronger board development

Actually, looking more carefully: Nimbus Maze + Swamp + Arcane Signet = 3 mana available. With 3 mana, they can cast either Dungeon Map (3) or Baleful Strix (UB = 2 mana, leaving 1 unused). Baleful Strix draws a card immediately, provides a relevant blocker with deathtouch and flying, and triggers Sefris's venture ability if it dies. Dungeon Map is a slow mana rock that won't provide meaningful value for several turns. Playing Baleful Strix would have been better — it replaces itself and provides board presence, while Dungeon Map is a tempo-negative play that doesn't impact the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Dungeon Map for 3 mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Baleful Strix for UB (2 mana), drawing a card immediately and deploying a flying deathtouch blocker, with 1 mana left over

With only 4 lands (and Boros Garrison in hand which would bounce one), the 6-mana Combustible Gearhulk is expensive but represents a powerful threat with first strike and card draw/damage. More importantly, discarding Combustible Gearhulk to the graveyard has strong synergy with Feldon of the Third Path (which is still in hand) - Feldon can reanimate a copy of Gearhulk for just 2R, getting its ETB trigger. Chain Reaction is a board wipe that currently has limited value since there are very few creatures on the battlefield. However, Boros Garrison is a tap-land that bounces a land and doesn't accelerate much in a deck that needs to get to 6 mana for Sun Titan. Discarding Boros Garrison instead of Combustible Gearhulk would have been better - the Gearhulk is a premium Feldon target and a strong card to cast naturally, while Boros Garrison is a mediocre land. Actually, keeping Combustible Gearhulk as a Feldon target makes the Gearhulk discard somewhat defensible since it goes to the graveyard where Feldon wants it. But discarding both Chain Reaction AND Combustible Gearhulk means losing a board wipe. The better line was to discard Boros Garrison (a tapped land that bounces another land, poor tempo) and either Chain Reaction or Battlemage's Bracers. Actually, re-reading: Combustible Gearhulk in the graveyard IS good with Feldon. And Chain Reaction has limited current utility. But Boros Garrison should have been a discard candidate over Chain Reaction since Chain Reaction is a board wipe that could be critical later, and Reconstruct History can get it back. The discard of Chain Reaction over Boros Garrison is the questionable part.

annotations.betterLine: Discard Boros Garrison (mediocre tapped bounce-land) and Combustible Gearhulk (which becomes a Feldon target in the graveyard). This preserves Chain Reaction as a board wipe option and still sets up the Feldon + Gearhulk synergy.

MiMo Timmy at 40hp has only 4 lands and no creatures on board - attacking MiMo would avoid the Propaganda tax entirely and apply pressure to a vulnerable opponent with a weak board state. Additionally, GPT5m Gramps has Baleful Strix (a 1/1 deathtouch flyer) that could block one attacker favorably.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Libby chose not to attack with Rootha (1/4) and Talrand (2/2) when there were viable targets. MiMo Timmy has no blockers and is at 40 life, and Llama4 Valley has no blockers either. GPT5m Gramps has Propaganda up which taxes attacks, but the other two players are open. While the damage is small (1-3 points), there's essentially no downside to attacking an undefended player — Rootha is a 1/4 that survives most combat and Talrand is a 2/2 that could chip in. The reasoning given ('lending fees remain usurious') references Propaganda but that only applies to attacking Gramps. Free damage should generally be taken in Commander, especially when it costs nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack MiMo Timmy (who has no blockers and no board presence) with Talrand, Sky Summoner and/or Rootha, Mercurial Artist for 2-3 free damage. Rootha could be kept back if you want the option to bounce it for spell copying, but Talrand has no reason not to swing.

annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Fiery Encore
annotations.betterLine: Discard Inferno Project, which is a 7-mana creature that would enter with very few counters given the sparse instant/sorcery graveyard, making it nearly useless.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps attacked with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch) into a board where Kimi25 Libby has Rootha, Mercurial Artist and Talrand, Sky Summoner. Baleful Strix is a valuable defensive piece - its deathtouch makes it an excellent blocker that deters attacks, and it synergizes with Phantom Steed in hand (exile it, get repeated ETB draws). With Propaganda already providing attack deterrence, the Strix is more valuable as a blocker/combo piece than as a 1-damage attacker. However, the 1 flying damage is free if nobody blocks, and Pramikon isn't on the battlefield to restrict attack directions, so the risk depends on who can block. Kimi25 Libby doesn't appear to have flying blockers currently, so the Strix would likely get through for 1. The risk is minimal but the upside is also minimal - 1 damage in a 4-player game at 37+ life totals is nearly irrelevant, while losing the Strix to any flash creature or combat trick would be bad.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Baleful Strix
annotations.betterLine: Hold back Baleful Strix as a deathtouch blocker and potential Phantom Steed target for card advantage. The 1 flying damage is negligible in multiplayer, and the Strix provides much more value on defense and as a combo piece with Phantom Steed.

annotations.description: During combat (on their own turn), Llama4 Valley chose to sacrifice Commander's Sphere to draw a card. Commander's Sphere is a mana rock that provides colored mana, and sacrificing it permanently removes a mana source. With expensive cards in hand like Zetalpa (8 mana) and only 8 lands/mana sources, losing a mana rock is significant. Additionally, this is their own combat step - they could use Oona's Grace (an instant) to draw a card by discarding a land, which is generally available from the graveyard via retrace anyway. More importantly, they could simply pass here and use Commander's Sphere for mana on future turns to cast their expensive spells, or at minimum wait until end of an opponent's turn to sacrifice it if they really want the card draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Sacrificed Commander's Sphere to draw a card during their own combat step
annotations.betterLine: Pass without activating either ability, preserving Commander's Sphere as a mana source to help cast expensive cards like Zetalpa, Primal Dawn (8 mana) and Pramikon, Sky Rampart. If card draw was needed, use Oona's Grace from graveyard instead, or at minimum wait until an opponent's end step to sacrifice the Sphere.

annotations.description: Casting Oona's Grace via Retrace during combat costs {2}{U} plus discarding Prairie Stream (a dual land). With 8 lands already in play, the land isn't critical, but spending 3 mana to draw 1 card at the cost of a land card is inefficient when they have multiple meaningful plays in hand (Pramikon at 3 mana, Ral Zarek at 4 mana, Gerrard at 4 mana) that they'll want mana for in main phase 2.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Oona's Grace via Retrace, discarding a land to draw one card during combat
annotations.betterLine: Save the mana for main phase 2 to deploy a meaningful permanent like Pramikon, Sky Rampart or Ral Zarek, or at minimum wait until end of opponent's turn to use mana if nothing better presents itself

annotations.description: Oona's Grace says 'Target player draws a card.' Llama4 Valley cast Oona's Grace with retrace (discarding Prairie Stream) but targeted GPT5m Gramps instead of themselves. This means they paid 2U + discarded a land to give an opponent a card draw. The reasoning suggests they thought this would 'disrupt' the opponent, but drawing a card is always beneficial for the recipient. Llama4 Valley essentially spent a land and mana to help an opponent while getting nothing themselves.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted GPT5m Gramps with Oona's Grace, giving the opponent a free card draw.
annotations.betterLine: Target themselves with Oona's Grace to draw a card, since the whole point of retracing Oona's Grace is card filtering/advantage for yourself.

annotations.description: The model admitted it couldn't identify what the two triggered abilities were and chose essentially at random. While trigger ordering decisions are often low-impact, making a blind choice without understanding what you're ordering could lead to suboptimal resolution order.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose one of two triggered abilities to stack first without understanding what either ability does.
annotations.betterLine: Should have identified the triggered abilities (likely from casting an instant/sorcery spell) and ordered them optimally based on which effect benefits from resolving first or last.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley cast Increasing Vengeance via Flashback (costing {3}{R}{R}) to copy Oona's Grace, which is an opponent's spell (Kimi25 Libby likely cast it). Increasing Vengeance can only target an instant or sorcery spell *you control*. Since Oona's Grace is not Llama4's spell, this is an illegal target, wasting the Flashback cast and exiling Increasing Vengeance for nothing. Even if the targeting were somehow valid, spending 5 mana and exiling a powerful spell from the graveyard just to copy a 'draw one card' spell is extremely poor value. The Commander's Sphere sacrifice (draw a card) or simply passing would have been far better uses of resources.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Increasing Vengeance from graveyard via Flashback targeting Oona's Grace (an opponent's spell), paying {3}{R}{R} and exiling Increasing Vengeance.
annotations.betterLine: Either sacrifice Commander's Sphere to draw a card, or simply pass without spending resources. Increasing Vengeance should be saved for copying one of your own high-value spells, not wasted on an opponent's cantrip (which is an illegal target anyway).

annotations.description: MiMo Timmy cast Battlemage's Bracers (2R) before considering whether to use Feldon's ability this turn. With 5 lands (4 Mountains + 1 Plains + 1 Secluded Steppe), casting Bracers costs 3 mana, leaving only 2 mana available. Feldon's ability costs 2R+tap, so Timmy can't both cast Bracers AND activate Feldon this turn. Furthermore, equipping Bracers costs another 2 mana, so even next turn it would require 5 mana just to equip and activate Feldon. Hedron Archive (4 generic) would have been a strong alternative - it provides ramp to enable Feldon activations on future turns more reliably, and can be sacrificed for card draw later. Alternatively, casting Thopter Engineer (2R) would create an artifact creature token and give artifact creatures haste, providing board presence. The Bracers are only valuable once equipped to Feldon and activated, which requires significant additional mana investment. However, Bracers + Feldon is a powerful combo that doubles his reanimation value, so planning ahead for it is defensible.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Battlemage's Bracers for 2R, leaving only 2 mana and unable to activate Feldon this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Hedron Archive (4 mana) for ramp, enabling Feldon activation next turn with more mana available, or cast Thopter Engineer for immediate board presence and haste for artifact creatures.

Rootha is more defensible to hold back (1 power, useful ability), but Talrand could have gotten in for 2 damage somewhere relatively safely.

The Titan token would threaten significant damage this combat. With remaining 2 mana, Mind Stone could have been cast for future ramp.

annotations.description: MiMo Timmy chose Thousand-Year Elixir as the artifact to return with Reconstruct History, but Triplicate Titan is a far superior choice. Triplicate Titan is a 9/9 with flying, vigilance, and trample that creates three 3/3 tokens when it dies. More importantly, MiMo has Feldon of the Third Path on the battlefield, which can already create temporary copies of creatures in the graveyard - so keeping Triplicate Titan in the graveyard for Feldon isn't necessarily better than having it in hand. Thousand-Year Elixir costs 3 mana and gives haste to activated abilities and can untap creatures - it has synergy with Feldon but is much lower impact than a 9/9 threat. Combustible Gearhulk would also be a strong choice as a 6/6 first striker with card draw/damage ETB. The reasoning in the decision even acknowledges Triplicate Titan is huge but then pivots away without good justification.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Thousand-Year Elixir as the artifact card to return with Reconstruct History
annotations.betterLine: Choose Triplicate Titan (or Combustible Gearhulk) as the artifact to return - these are high-impact threats that can win the game, whereas Thousand-Year Elixir is a support piece with marginal value given the current board state

annotations.description: Call the Skybreaker has Retrace, meaning it can be cast from the graveyard by discarding a land card. Discarding it to hand size actually makes it MORE accessible since it can be reused from the graveyard. However, Sol Ring costs only {1} and produces 2 mana - it's one of the most powerful cards in Commander and should have been played long ago (it only costs 1 mana). The real issue is that Sol Ring is still in hand on turn 15, and rather than discarding a less impactful card, the player chose Call the Skybreaker. While Call the Skybreaker with Retrace is fine to discard, the bigger problem is that Sol Ring should have been cast this turn or earlier. Looking at the board, Kimi25 Libby has 6 lands and Rootha + Talrand untapped - they had mana available to cast Sol Ring ({1}) at some point. Additionally, discarding Elemental Masterpiece would have been better since it has a discard ability that creates a Treasure token ({U/R}{U/R}, discard: create Treasure), but that requires paying mana. Actually, Call the Skybreaker with Retrace from graveyard is arguably better positioned there than in hand, so this discard isn't terrible. The real blunder is having Sol Ring in hand on turn 15 - but since the decision point is specifically about the discard, and Call the Skybreaker is actually a reasonable discard due to Retrace, the main issue is not discarding something less useful. Traumatic Visions or Talisman of Creativity could have been discarded instead, but Sol Ring at 1 mana should have been cast, and keeping it in hand to cast next turn is correct. Call the Skybreaker with Retrace from graveyard is actually a fine discard choice.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Call the Skybreaker while still holding Sol Ring on turn 15
annotations.betterLine: Sol Ring should have been cast earlier in the turn (it costs only {1}), then discard would be from 7 cards. Call the Skybreaker is actually a reasonable retrace discard, but having Sol Ring uncast on turn 15 represents significant lost tempo across the game.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is attacking with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch) into a board where they have Propaganda protecting them. The Strix is a valuable defensive piece - it has deathtouch and flying, making it an excellent blocker that deters attacks. Attacking with it exposes it to potential blocks or removal, and the 1 damage is fairly insignificant in a 4-player game where opponents are at 28-39 life. Additionally, the attack direction matters - they need to attack someone specific, and 1 damage is negligible. However, Baleful Strix has already drawn its card, and with flying it's unlikely to be blocked profitably. The deathtouch flying body is still useful as a deterrent blocker though, and losing it to a combat trick or unexpected block would be unfortunate. This is debatable - the 1 chip damage has some value, but keeping the deathtouch blocker back is also reasonable, especially when GPT5m Gramps is at 28 life and relying on Propaganda for defense.

annotations.betterLine: Hold back Baleful Strix as a deathtouch flying blocker to complement Propaganda's defensive strategy, especially since 1 damage is negligible and the defensive value of deathtouch is significant

annotations.description: MiMo Timmy has 6 lands (4 Mountains, 1 Plains, 1 Secluded Steppe) plus Feldon of the Third Path on the battlefield. The key issue is that Mind Stone is a 2-mana rock when they already have 6 lands and could instead be casting Sun Titan (4WW = 6 mana). Sun Titan is a 6/6 vigilance that returns permanents with MV 3 or less from graveyard to battlefield - it could bring back Thousand-Year Elixir (which synergizes amazingly with Feldon by letting him activate twice), Boros Garrison (ramp), or other key pieces. MiMo's mana is 4 Mountains + 1 Plains + 1 Secluded Steppe = they can produce 4R + 1W + 1W = 4RWW. Sun Titan costs 4WW, which is exactly castable with this mana. Playing Mind Stone instead means Sun Titan gets delayed a turn while providing minimal benefit since they already have enough mana for their key plays.

Playing the land is fine, but Sol Ring should have been cast as well - they had the mana to do both. Looking at the choices, Sol Ring costs {1} and they have untapped lands available. annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps discarded Sunblast Angel, a powerful 4/5 flyer that destroys all tapped creatures on ETB. However, Eternal Dragon has plainscycling to help find lands, and Fellwar Stone helps ramp, so keeping those makes sense. The real question is whether Sunblast Angel or Meteor Golem should be discarded - Sunblast Angel is generally stronger since it's a one-sided wipe against aggressive opponents (destroying tapped creatures after combat), while Meteor Golem destroys any single nonland permanent. With Llama4 Valley being the only remaining opponent with River Kelpie on board, Sunblast Angel could be a game-changer if the Kelpie attacks and becomes tapped.

annotations.description: In a 1v1 against Llama4 Valley at 39 life, GPT5m Gramps chose to cast Rod of Absorption ({2}{U}) instead of playing a land and deploying Sun Titan (6 mana), which would immediately return a permanent with MV 3 or less from their stacked graveyard (Baleful Strix, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, etc.) and present a 6/6 vigilance threat. Rod of Absorption is a slow setup card that does nothing immediately in a 1v1 endgame where board presence matters far more.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Rod of Absorption for {2}{U}
annotations.betterLine: Play a land (Island or Plains), then cast Sun Titan for {4}{W}{W}, triggering its ETB to return a key permanent like Baleful Strix or Arcane Signet from graveyard, establishing a dominant board presence.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Grave Endeavor, a 7-mana instant that reanimates a creature with +1/+1 counters and drains opponents. With a graveyard full of powerful creatures (Ashen Rider, Sun Titan, Karmic Guide, Meteor Golem, Sunblast Angel, etc.), Grave Endeavor would be an extremely powerful spell if cast. However, the player also has Unburial Rites in hand (which has flashback) and Sun Titan, both of which serve reanimation purposes. The key issue is that Grave Endeavor is an instant (castable at instant speed) and provides both reanimation AND life drain, making it arguably stronger than some alternatives to discard. That said, they're keeping both Sun Titan and Unburial Rites which together provide strong reanimation redundancy, and with only 6 lands in play, casting the 7-mana Grave Endeavor would take a while. Discarding a land like one of the Plains might have been better since they already have limited colored mana sources and Unburial Rites' flashback only needs white, while keeping the powerful instant for later. But with Rod of Absorption also in hand (which could exile instants/sorceries), the decision is debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Grave Endeavor to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the two Plains instead, keeping Grave Endeavor as a powerful instant-speed reanimation spell that also drains opponents. With Unburial Rites already providing sorcery-speed reanimation (with flashback), Grave Endeavor adds instant-speed flexibility and the life drain component could matter in the endgame.

annotations.description: Casting Wall of Omens before playing a land means GPT5m Gramps goes from 8 cards in hand to 7 (cast) then 8 (draw from Wall), requiring a discard to 7. If they played a land first (going to 7 cards), then cast Wall of Omens (6 cards), then drew (7 cards), they'd avoid discarding entirely and have more mana available for whatever they draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wall of Omens before playing a land for the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Plains or Island for untapped mana, or Arcane Sanctum), then cast Wall of Omens to avoid needing to discard and to have more mana available for any drawn card

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Wall of Omens over a basic land. Wall of Omens is a 2-mana creature that draws a card on ETB, which has excellent synergy with Sun Titan (which can return it from the graveyard since it has MV 2), Karmic Guide, Unburial Rites, and other reanimation effects already in the graveyard. However, the player already has Sun Titan and Unburial Rites in hand as reanimation tools, and Wall of Omens in the graveyard is actually a fine Sun Titan target. The real issue is that they should discard one of the three basic lands (two Plains and an Island) instead, since they already have 6 lands on the battlefield and multiple lands in hand. A basic Plains would be the most expendable card - they already have Port Town and Nimbus Maze for white mana, and keeping Wall of Omens in hand allows casting it for value rather than relying on reanimation to get the draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Wall of Omens instead of a basic land
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Plains - GPT5m Gramps has two Plains and an Island in hand plus Arcane Sanctum, which is excessive land. Wall of Omens is a cheap cantrip creature that provides value whether cast from hand or reanimated by Sun Titan.

annotations.description: Attacking with all 4 creatures into Propaganda costs 8 mana (4×2), using all available mana and leaving nothing for interaction spells like Leadership Vacuum (2U) or Desperate Ravings (1R). The attack deals 20 to a 25-life opponent, which isn't lethal either way.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all creatures (Zetalpa, Pristine Skywise, Elsha, River Kelpie), paying 8 mana for Propaganda tax
annotations.betterLine: Attack with just Zetalpa and Pristine Skywise for 14 damage (4 mana Propaganda tax), keeping 4 mana open for interaction like Leadership Vacuum or Desperate Ravings. The extra 6 damage from Elsha and River Kelpie doesn't achieve lethal and leaves you completely tapped out.

annotations.description: Leadership Vacuum is a narrow instant that returns commanders to the command zone and draws a card. In this game state, Llama4 Valley has Pramikon on board (their own commander), and the only other living opponent is GPT5m Gramps who has no commander on the battlefield. However, Leadership Vacuum still cantrips (draws a card) for 3 mana, making it a cheap interaction piece. Meanwhile, Boros Guildgate and Mystic Monastery are tap-lands that could help fix mana, and the player already has 8 lands with decent color coverage. Discarding Boros Guildgate (a tap-land entering tapped that only produces R/W, colors already well-covered) would likely be better than discarding a cantripping interaction spell. Even if Leadership Vacuum's primary mode is less useful with no opposing commanders in play, the card replacement aspect gives it some floor value.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Leadership Vacuum
annotations.betterLine: Discard Boros Guildgate or Mystic Monastery, as these are redundant tap-lands when the player already has 8 lands, while Leadership Vacuum at least cantrips and could be relevant if GPT5m Gramps replays their commander.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley passed priority during combat without using available instant-speed card draw. With 8 lands on the battlefield (enough mana available), they could have cast Think Twice (1U) or Desperate Ravings (1R) from hand to draw cards at end of combat or during this phase, using mana that would otherwise go unused. Think Twice also has flashback value later. Chemister's Insight (3U) was also castable. Drawing cards at instant speed during combat (or at end of opponent's turn) is pure upside when mana is available and going unused.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any instant-speed card draw spells despite having available mana and multiple options.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice or Desperate Ravings using available mana to draw cards, since this mana would likely go unused otherwise. These are best cast at end of turn or during combat to maximize information before committing.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is in a 1v1 situation against Llama4 Valley (the other two players are eliminated at negative life). With only 6 lands in play (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Port Town, Propaganda, Dungeon Map, Lightning Greaves - only 3 actual mana-producing lands plus artifacts), GPT5m Gramps desperately needs to reanimate threats. Rod of Absorption is a 3-mana artifact that's very slow and situational - it needs to be deployed, then accumulate exiled spells, then sacrificed. Meanwhile, discarding a land (Plains or Island) would be much better since the hand already has Unburial Rites (which can be cast from graveyard with flashback for 3W), Sun Titan (which can recur permanents), and Victimize. The reanimation plan is the clear path to victory. Discarding a Plains would actually help since Unburial Rites has white flashback cost and Sun Titan could recur it from the graveyard. However, Rod of Absorption is genuinely weak here in a late-game 1v1 with limited mana, so discarding it isn't terrible. The real issue is that discarding one of the extra Plains copies would be strictly better - they have two Plains in hand plus Arcane Sanctum, and the Plains are less useful than Rod of Absorption which at least has some theoretical upside.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Rod of Absorption
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Plains instead. With two Plains, an Island, and Arcane Sanctum in hand, one Plains is redundant. Rod of Absorption, while slow, is at least a unique effect that could provide value if the game goes long, whereas an extra basic land when you already have multiple lands to play is less valuable.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps cast Doomed Necromancer (a 3-mana creature that needs to survive a turn cycle to activate) before playing a land. They have Plains, Island, and Arcane Sanctum in hand but only 6 lands on the battlefield (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Propaganda uses no land slot, Port Town, Dungeon Map, Lightning Greaves - actually only Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Port Town are lands plus some artifacts). More critically, casting Doomed Necromancer with only 3 mana available (if that) means they can't also play a land and advance their mana development. They should play a land first before casting spells. Additionally, with Sun Titan and Unburial Rites in hand alongside powerful reanimation targets in the graveyard (Ashen Rider, Karmic Guide, Meteor Golem, Sunblast Angel), the better play would be to play a land (Arcane Sanctum or Plains) to build toward casting Unburial Rites (4B) or Sun Titan (4WW) next turn. Doomed Necromancer requires surviving a full turn cycle AND having B mana available, making it slow and vulnerable compared to just casting Unburial Rites when they have enough mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Doomed Necromancer before playing a land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Arcane Sanctum for color fixing, or Plains), then cast Doomed Necromancer if still desired. Prioritizing land drops to reach Unburial Rites or Sun Titan mana sooner would be more impactful.

annotations.description: Discarding Island instead of a duplicate Plains loses blue mana access. With Nimbus Maze on the battlefield (which produces U only if you control a Plains, and W only if you control an Island), keeping the Island is valuable since they already have two Plains and Arcane Sanctum for white mana. Playing an Island would let Nimbus Maze tap for U, providing better color diversity.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Island
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the two Plains instead, keeping the Island for blue mana diversity and to enable Nimbus Maze to produce U.

annotations.description: Thalia's Geistcaller has strong synergy with Llama4 Valley's graveyard-heavy strategy (many flashback spells in graveyard like Sevinne's Reclamation, Ignite the Future, Divine Reckoning, etc.), creating spirit tokens and providing lifelink. Boros Guildgate is a tapped land providing R/W colors already available from existing lands.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Thalia's Geistcaller
annotations.betterLine: Discard Boros Guildgate, which enters tapped and provides colors already covered by existing lands. Thalia's Geistcaller would generate significant value with the many flashback spells available in the graveyard.

annotations.description: Reassembling Skeleton is a recursive creature that can return itself from the graveyard to the battlefield for {1}{B}, making it arguably better in the graveyard than in hand. However, GPT5m Gramps has powerful reanimation spells (Unburial Rites, Victimize, Sun Titan) and reanimation targets (Ashen Rider, Karmic Guide, Meteor Golem, Sunblast Angel) in the graveyard. Discarding Reassembling Skeleton is reasonable since it functions from the graveyard, but discarding a Plains instead could be considered since they already have lands on the battlefield and Plains in the graveyard. The Skeleton does serve as a sacrifice outlet for Victimize, which is relevant. On the other hand, keeping both Plains ensures land drops for future turns to cast expensive spells like Sun Titan (6 mana) and Unburial Rites (5 mana). With only 6 lands in play, land drops are still important. Discarding the Skeleton is defensible since it works from the graveyard, but a Plains could have been discarded instead since they have multiple Plains already.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Reassembling Skeleton
annotations.betterLine: Discarding a Plains instead, since GPT5m already has Plains on board and in graveyard, while keeping Reassembling Skeleton in hand preserves the option to cast it as a creature for Victimize sacrifice fodder without spending the {1}{B} recursion cost. Though the Skeleton does function from graveyard, having it in hand gives more flexibility.

annotations.description: GPT5m Gramps is discarding down to hand size and chose to discard Necrotic Sliver. While Necrotic Sliver isn't the strongest card in hand, it's a creature that could be reanimated from the graveyard (which is fine since they have reanimation spells). However, the real question is whether discarding a Plains or Arcane Sanctum would have been better. They already have very few lands on the battlefield (only 4 mana-producing lands: Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Port Town, plus Dungeon Map for colorless) and desperately need to play lands to cast their expensive spells like Sun Titan (6 mana) and Unburial Rites (5 mana). Keeping both Plains and Arcane Sanctum seems correct for land drops. Necrotic Sliver is a reasonable discard since it can be reanimated later and is less impactful than the reanimation package (Victimize, Unburial Rites, Doomed Necromancer, Sun Titan). The discard is defensible but one could argue that Doomed Necromancer might be better to discard since it also goes to the graveyard where it can be reanimated, and Necrotic Sliver's sacrifice-to-destroy ability is quite strong in this board state where Llama4 Valley has threats like Zetalpa and Pramikon.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Necrotic Sliver
annotations.betterLine: Discard is reasonable since Necrotic Sliver can be reanimated later, but discarding a Plains instead could also be justified since they already have Plains in graveyard for potential recursion and Necrotic Sliver's destroy ability is very relevant against Llama4 Valley's board.

annotations.description: Desperate Ravings has flashback {2}{U}, meaning it can be cast from the graveyard for value later (draw 2, discard 1 at random). With Llama4 Valley running a graveyard-synergy deck (River Kelpie triggers on graveyard casts, Sevinne's Reclamation, etc.), flashback cards in the graveyard are valuable resources. Meanwhile, Azorius Locket is a 3-mana rock that's mediocre at this stage when they already have 7+ lands, and Azorius Chancery is a tapland that bounces a land. Either of those would be less impactful discards than a flashback spell.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Desperate Ravings, a card with flashback that synergizes with their graveyard strategy.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Azorius Locket or Azorius Chancery instead, as they provide less future value than a flashback spell in a deck that benefits from casting spells from the graveyard.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley has flashback spells available and mana open during combat (likely end of turn timing). Think Twice (flashback {2}{U}) and Desperate Ravings (flashback {2}{U}) could be cast from the graveyard to draw cards, and Oona's Grace could be cast with retrace by discarding a land. With 9 lands on the battlefield (including Temple of the False God), there's likely enough mana to cast at least one of these card-draw spells. Passing priority without using available mana sinks wastes potential card advantage, especially since this appears to be an end-of-turn window where unused mana would go to waste.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells, leaving mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice from graveyard for its flashback cost ({2}{U}) or Desperate Ravings from graveyard for its flashback cost ({2}{U}) to draw cards with otherwise unused mana.

annotations.description: Mystic Retrieval returns a target instant or sorcery from graveyard to hand. Ignite the Future costs 3R and exiles top 3 cards to play until end of next turn, but with only 8 lands (some tapped) and needing to recast it, the value is uncertain. Meanwhile, Sevinne's Reclamation (2W, flashback 4W) could return a permanent with MV 3 or less from graveyard to battlefield - potentially getting back Burning Vengeance, Burnished Hart, Command Tower, or other valuable permanents. Deep Analysis (flashback 1U, pay 3 life) could also be retrieved for efficient card draw. Think Twice is cheap flashback draw. The choice of Ignite the Future is defensible as a high-ceiling play, but given the current board state with only Pramikon as a real permanent and needing to rebuild, Sevinne's Reclamation would likely provide more consistent value by recurring key permanents like Burning Vengeance or Dockside Extortionist directly to the battlefield.
annotations.actionTaken: Retrieved Ignite the Future with Mystic Retrieval
annotations.betterLine: Retrieve Sevinne's Reclamation to recur key low-MV permanents like Burning Vengeance, Dockside Extortionist, or Command Tower from the graveyard to the battlefield, providing more reliable board development

annotations.description: Chose Red for protection color when the only remaining opponent (GPT5m Gramps) plays WUB colors with no red sources. Red protection is useless here.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Red for protection color
annotations.betterLine: Should have chosen White or Black, which are the colors of the opponent's removal spells (Swords to Plowshares, Despark, Utter End in graveyard) and permanents.

annotations.description: Discarding Azorius Chancery (a land) when the player has 8 lands in play and several high-impact cards in hand. While Azorius Chancery entering tapped and bouncing a land is a tempo hit, it still provides mana fixing (W/U) and net mana advantage over time. With only 8 lands and expensive cards like Ignite the Future (flashback 7R), Pristine Angel (4WW), and Devil's Play (X+R, flashback X+RRR) in hand, more mana sources could be valuable. However, the bounce-a-land drawback makes it the weakest land option, and cards like Jace's Sanctum, Ghostly Prison, and Talrand are all quite strong in this position.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Azorius Chancery
annotations.betterLine: Could argue for discarding Devil's Play instead, since with limited red mana sources (only 1 Mountain + Temple) and expensive flashback cost (X+RRR), it's unlikely to deal significant damage. However, Devil's Play is a flexible win condition. Azorius Chancery is a reasonable discard given the tempo loss of bouncing a land, so this is debatable rather than clearly wrong.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley passed priority during the combat step without using available instant-speed card draw. Think Twice (flashback {2}{U}) and Desperate Ravings (flashback {2}{U}) are both available from the graveyard, and with 8 lands on the battlefield (including Temple of the False God for {C}{C}), there's mana available to cast at least one of these at end of turn or during combat. While passing here isn't terrible since they could use mana on their own turn, using flashback spells at instant speed during opponents' turns is generally better to keep mana open during your own turn for more options.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any instant-speed spells.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice from graveyard for its flashback cost ({2}{U}) or Desperate Ravings from graveyard ({2}{U}) to draw cards at instant speed while the mana would otherwise go unused.

annotations.description: With 39 life and likely 10+ mana available (including Temple of the False God), Storm Herd would create 39 1/1 flying Pegasus tokens, essentially winning the game against the sole remaining opponent (GPT5m Gramps at 25 life with only Propaganda for defense). Even with Propaganda requiring 2 mana per attacker, sending just 13 tokens through next turn would be lethal. Instead, Valley cast a 2/2 creature that provides incremental value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Talrand, Sky Summoner (4 mana), a 2/2 that creates Drake tokens when casting instants/sorceries
annotations.betterLine: Cast Storm Herd ({8}{W}{W}) to create 39 1/1 flying Pegasus tokens, which would be lethal on the next attack against the sole remaining opponent at 25 life, even accounting for Propaganda costs.

With only two opponents remaining (both at negative life - though that seems like a tracking issue, they're likely still alive), drawing cards to find action is important. Additionally, Chemister's Insight could be cast via jump-start by discarding a card. Passing here wastes available mana that could generate card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells from the graveyard despite having mana available.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice from graveyard for {2}{U} to draw a card, and potentially also cast Desperate Ravings from graveyard for {2}{U} to draw more cards, using the available mana productively before moving to other phases.

With two opponents eliminated and only GPT5m Gramps remaining at 25 life, drawing into more resources is valuable, and there's no reason to hold up mana when these are pure card advantage at instant speed.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any instant-speed spells
annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice or Desperate Ravings from graveyard using flashback to draw cards with unused mana, since these are instant-speed and it's the postcombat main phase with mana available

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley is discarding down to 7 cards and chose to discard Pristine Angel, a 4/4 flying creature with strong protection abilities. However, with only 9 lands (including Temple of the False God) and needing colored mana, the hand contains several expensive spells. Pristine Angel costs 4WW which is castable with current lands. Storm Herd (8WW) is extremely expensive and likely uncastable for many turns - it would be a more natural discard. That said, Pristine Angel competes with Zetalpa as a flying finisher and Valley already has Pramikon out, so the protection from colors while untapped is less critical. Storm Herd could be game-winning if Valley reaches enough mana given their 39 life total, making 39 1/1 flying Pegasus tokens. The choice between discarding Storm Herd vs Pristine Angel is debatable - Storm Herd is a potential game-ender but very expensive, while Pristine Angel is more reliably castable but less impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Pristine Angel
annotations.betterLine: Discard Storm Herd, which costs 10 mana and is unlikely to be cast soon, while keeping Pristine Angel as a more castable threat with strong protective abilities

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley passed priority during combat without using available mana sinks or flashback spells. With 9 lands (including Temple of the False God for 2 mana), they could have cast Think Twice from the graveyard for {2}{U} to draw a card at instant speed, or Desperate Ravings from the graveyard for {2}{U} to draw cards. These are pure value plays at instant speed that cost nothing strategically to use during combat or at end of turn. Missing the opportunity to use mana on flashback card draw when it's available is leaving value on the table.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spells or using any abilities.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Think Twice from graveyard (flashback {2}{U}) or Desperate Ravings from graveyard (flashback {2}{U}) to draw cards at instant speed, using otherwise wasted mana.

annotations.description: Llama4 Valley is in a 1v1 situation against GPT5m Gramps (25hp) with both Kimi25 Libby and MiMo Timmy eliminated. Valley has 39 life and only Pramikon on board but has 8 lands (7 untapped after Swiftwater Cliffs is tapped). They have flashback spells available in graveyard and cards like Think Twice, Desperate Ravings, and Chemister's Insight that could be cast from graveyard to dig for action. With Temple of the False God providing 2 mana, they have access to significant mana. Casting Think Twice from graveyard (flashback {2}{U}) or Desperate Ravings from graveyard (flashback {2}{U}) during their own main phase would help find threats or answers. More importantly, they should be deploying threats - they could cast Backdraft Hellkite (3RR) which would be excellent as it gives all instants/sorceries in graveyard flashback when it attacks. They have the mana for it with Mountain + Temple of the False God + Islands. Passing without doing anything in main phase wastes development time.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting anything during precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Backdraft Hellkite for {3}{R}{R} using Mountain, Temple of the False God, and Islands (via Pramikon's color identity allowing the mana). Alternatively, at minimum cast Think Twice or Desperate Ravings from graveyard to draw cards and develop board position against the remaining opponent.

Darkwater Catacombs would have provided access to black and blue mana needed for key reanimation spells like Unburial Rites, Victimize, and Doomed Necromancer.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Darkwater Catacombs
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the two Plains, since Arcane Sanctum already provides white mana and the deck desperately needs black mana sources for its reanimation package.
